title: High CPU or Memory Usage / OOM-Killer Triggered
symptom: Instance is sluggish, SSH sessions lag, and backend process dies unexpectedly with exit code 137.
initial_observations: dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Kill process'.
environment: EC2 t3.small or t3.medium instance running memory-intensive workloads.

possible_causes.cause: Memory leak in application process causing OS Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer invocation
possible_causes.evidence_needed: dmesg logs showing 'kernel: Out of memory: Kill process <PID> (<name>) score <score>'.
possible_causes.remediation: Restart service, analyze heap dumps, configure swap file as buffer, and scale instance RAM size.
Identify thread deadlock or infinite loop; restart worker and patch bug.

investigation_steps.title: Check Real-Time Memory and Process Consumption
investigation_steps.explanation: Inspect total, used, and available RAM and top memory consuming processes.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Available memory near 0, process consuming majority of memory.

investigation_steps.title: Check Kernel Ring Buffer for OOM Killer Events
investigation_steps.command: sudo dmesg -T | grep -iE 'oom|out of memory|killed process' | tail -15
investigation_steps.explanation: Look for explicit Linux kernel OOM killer actions and process termination records.

verification: free -h shows healthy available memory and application is running without OOM kills.
prevention: Enable swap space on EBS volume for burst absorption.
Configure memory limits via systemd cgroups (MemoryMax=...).
